notes.title: Patch 1.4.0
notes.content:
Alright, patch time! Not the biggest content drop ever but something quite interesting at least.

The biggest changes are an addition of a side boat that can hold an extra crew member of any position and two new crew members, Bungle the Jester and Baggy the Porter.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45266796/c3b4139b4593db0ec30aa24b903858e9b952456f.gif[/img]

Bungle was actually designed as more of an required addition to enemy arsenal as a bird deterrant but of course he serves a purpose on player side as well.

Baggy is the new addition to crow's nest position member pool. He isn't anything crazy overpowered but surely can be a worthy crew member in the right hands.

As a nice quality of life thing I added the option to skip to specific pages of the log book from the table of contents pages.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45266796/938b7f5306f80712ec8f904372c6e613908185c9.gif[/img]

There are also few new additional challenge modes on top of the existing price one.

And of course some generic/smaller bug fixes:

- Removed jumping to uncollector ship to hopefully resolve the random crashes there
- Added few new potential wishes
- Shortened overflowing sage tip
- Fixed autoplay battle going on in background on a restart
- Improved zooming/framing in some scenarios

notes.title: Patch 1.3.5
notes.content:
This patch is mainly focused on improving the performance of the game. The primary way to achieve this is the addition of a max limit to your visible cargo. When the cargo amount exceeds the limit, a special dice will appear which can be used to navigate between different cargo "pages".

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45266796/31dbcb23e0c3c19e7a683771c41028e8975b01a8.gif[/img]

This change is purely visual so splash damage for example can happen between pages if it is triggered on the edge. The cargo limit is 36 by default but that along with some other additional performance increasing options can be found through the menu.

In addition to reducing the lag caused by having so many dice, it also helps you reach the dice further back in your ship that would have been off screen before.

Of course I also fixed some bugs:

- Glow trinket no longer triggers on plated cargo
- Perl cargo (and other usable) can now be used if gained through bribing
- Blocked pearl usage after already lost
- Fixed issue where you can quickly select multiple cargo pieces as shot target
- Fixed some enemy divine crew member descriptions
- Increased delay between sacrifice/gain on wishes to better ensure the addition

notes.title: Patch 1.3.0
notes.content:
And here it is again, a fresh patch. Maybe a few days earlier than I had planned but so many bug reports kept coming in from issues that I had already fixed and didn't really want to bother releasing those fixes by themselves.

There isn't actually that much few content in this patch. It mainly focuses in introducing a cabin in your ship you can enter at almost any time and there you can read the captain's log book. The log book opens up as you play offering more details and hints on stuff you've seen.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45266796/fbbbf7b4e1cc634861c402cb87630f139e1b0ea2.gif[/img]

But it's not just a source of information either! There you can also pick a crew member and trinkets to start your run with. But of course you have to earn those starters first.

As always, let me know if you find and bugs and how you're liking the new feature. Happy sailing!

There you can also pick a crew member and trinkets to start your run with.

notes.title: Patch 1.2.5
notes.content:
Even more fixes are here! Let’s see… there’s quite a lot here, though most of them are nothing major.

The Genie event got a pretty major buff. The letter pool was increased from 9 to a whopping 16, allowing for more choices when making wishes. Additionally, some new trigger words have been added to the list of possible wishes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45266796/e4399986ed0e89d31ba5202806eb1163bfc62625.gif[/img]

The Clam Boss was getting heavily weakened by defensive crew members or trinkets, making it possible to completely negate its damage to pearls. Now, while defense still applies, it won’t fully block the boss’s attack on pearls anymore.

Finally solved the mystery of players ending up with seemingly blank dice cargo. Turns out, this was caused by splash damage (most likely from rigged cargo) occurring outside of combat — what a weirdly specific combination!

Introducing these two new friendly sky puppies! As if birds weren’t already too strong, these ones are even harder to obtain but deal more damage than normal ones. I might need to design a new boss specifically to counter mass bird builds...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45266796/332d6021b3ded38e883e807c4d89d9424a1d8f3b.gif[/img]

Figureheads had their fair share of issues too. The Handler one didn’t even work at all, and some had weird coloration problems, which should now be fixed. In some rare cases, it was also possible to stack multiple Figureheads, which is definitely not intended — or at least, not yet.

Rescuing the Prince had become way too rare due to all the new events, making it much less likely to encounter the King afterward. The chance of encountering the King (after acquiring the Prince) has now been significantly increased, so it’s no longer a near-impossible gamble.

Fishing got a big improvement. It’s now much faster, and you don’t need to be as quick to pull up the fish. Just standing around waiting isn’t very fun, so the wait time has been cut down to make things more engaging.

The math event was incorrectly displaying random(ish) values on mid-calculation dice when they were on the host ship. The dice still had the correct values, but they displayed incorrectly.

And then for just a list of rest of the minor fixes:

- Rewind event chance is now no longer affected by the Mark trinket.
- Fixed Spy stealing the last cargo piece from an enemy after a Rewind event.
- Fixed some crew ability stacking issues (like Swabbie +1 damage reduction).
- Gave Broom hair instead of a hat.
- The shoot button now only appears once the birds have finished their actions.
- Fixed Teenage Mutant Ninja Frog names not displaying properly.
- Fixed some dice color flashing issues.
- Fixed a rare issue where divine battles could lock up and prevent the player from shooting.

notes.title: Patch 1.2.3
notes.content:
A few more minor bug fixes...

Fixed an issue where the Skeleton Bard crew member could affect its own level. It was gaining an extra perk even when not yet upgraded, but this wasn’t reflected in the tooltip.

Fixed a visual glitch affecting Handler and Tinkerer when they were equipped with a sword. This happened after the event where you pick one of two crew members, and the next enemy receives the other.

Slightly nerfed the enemy Mate and Cabin Boy crew members when encountered early on (due to the same crew-picking event). The amount of cargo they provide now scales down based on how early in the game the encounter occurs.

Addressed a potential soft lock caused by the Rewind Pearl event, which could lead to the next enemy encounter having no cargo at all. This could cause issues, such as the Spy being sent to steal from a ship with nothing to take. Now, it should be impossible for enemies to have no cargo at all, preventing this issue.

notes.title: Patch 1.2.2
notes.content:
Here are even more bug fixes on top of the previous big patch.

Some small adjustments were made that don't affect gameplay much—like unifying trinket names to fix inconsistencies and adjusting the colors of fish/rigged cargo when plated or spiced. Also, the Figurehead crew member had a habit of "waking up" unexpectedly—that’s now fixed.

A potential crash/freeze could occur when encountering a crew change event with an over-leveled crew member. The game attempted to match the opponent’s crew to the same level but wasn’t allowing it properly. That’s now been resolved.

Stealing the only cargo from the Clam Boss is no longer possible. The effect was simply too powerful, completely nullifying an intended endgame challenge. Additionally, the same trinket was triggering on parrots dealing damage. While that didn’t impact gameplay much, it’s now fixed. Speaking of parrots, they were incorrectly duplicating when their handler visited the opponent’s ship and returned—that’s also been patched.

The Trinketinator can no longer be triggered multiple times before resolving, preventing an exploit where you could farm infinite trinkets for a single lost crew member. A small visual glitch when selecting Trinketinator targets has also been fixed.

The Spy upgrade was sometimes wasted when you had Figurehead, since Figurehead is always upgraded and couldn't be improved further. Now, the spying choice occurs after parrots have attacked, preventing errors where you’d attempt to spy on a ship that no longer exists or get stuck inside a sinking ship.

Finally, Divine Being battles have been tweaked to better account for the player's possible damage rolls. The difficulty still increases with more available options, but now there should be fewer unwinnable scenarios.

notes.title: Patch 1.2.1
notes.content:
What's a patch without the need for a small day-one fix on top of it? This update addresses three major issues introduced in the previous patch.

For those unaware, there's a new boss(-ish) battle where the enemy has a big plated die that can be repaired. That was all fine—except for one problem: there was a limit preventing cargo dice from being repaired past a value of 9. This restriction still applied during the boss fight, even if the die originally had a value higher than 9, severely lowering its max HP. This has now been fixed.

Next, let's talk about Spy’s sabotage ability. Spy can rig cargo dice, causing them to deal splash damage to nearby cargo when shot. However, I didn’t account for two rigged dice being next to each other—leading to an infinite damage loop that could pretty much crash the game. Now, rigged dice no longer take splash damage, preventing the chaos.

Finally, there was a bit of an oopsie with divine battles sometimes failing to end properly, which could soft-lock your run. That shouldn’t happen anymore. Even if you "lose" the challenge, you’ll still be able to leave—though slightly worse for wear.

notes.title: Patch 1.2.0
notes.content:
Finally, it's time to push this patch out! It’s the biggest one yet—though maybe not as big as one might expect, considering how long it took. I made the slight mistake of diving into the Terraria Calamity mod and Valheim while working on this update, and, unsurprisingly, they ended up being massive time sinks. Still, the patch is now complete enough for release—just in time before my next distraction drops on Friday.

This update brings quite a lot of new content. Most of it comes in the form of new event types, adding even more variety to each run. The endgame has also seen some major changes—events will continue happening post-end, but enemies will grow significantly tougher. Some events are even exclusive to the late game, offering major challenges to tackle.

May I introduce our two newest crew members: Handy, the parrot handler, and Spy, the... well, spy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45266796/d66bbe8fb3069f350535933af8695269aeac888e.gif[/img]

Handy provides you with some flying friends who help dish out extra damage in battles. Spy, on the other hand, can be sent on sabotage and investigation missions aboard enemy ships.

Beyond these two new crew types, every existing crew member now has two new variations, each with a little extra twist—similar to the frog variants.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45266796/abf7a70a3389f4ba31758e1c3ecd0cc13834843f.gif[/img]

As I mentioned earlier, there are plenty of new events in this patch. I won’t spoil them all, so get out there and discover them for yourself! Of course, there’s also a handful of new trinkets to find.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45266796/960f50b8c8d956d14366d434456e1c1a56312939.gif[/img]

And what would a patch be without a bunch of bug fixes and balance changes? Naturally, some new bugs will come along for the ride, so please let me know if (or rather, when) you find them!
